scenarios.situation: You are at a language meetup. Someone asks who you are.
scenarios.task: Say your name, where you are from, and what you do.

scenarios.situation: You are at a café counter.
scenarios.task: Order a coffee and a sandwich politely.

scenarios.situation: You are lost near the centre of town.
scenarios.task: Ask where the station is, then ask how much a ticket costs.

scenarios.situation: A friend asks about food.
scenarios.task: Say one thing you like eating and one thing you don't.

scenarios.situation: A colleague asks about your weekend plans.
scenarios.task: Say what you are going to do and who with.

scenarios.situation: Someone is speaking too fast.
scenarios.task: Say you don't understand and ask them to repeat more slowly.

scenarios.situation: A friend invites you to dinner on Friday. You have to work late.
scenarios.task: Decline politely and give the reason.

scenarios.situation: You and a friend want to meet this week.
scenarios.task: Suggest a day, a time and a place, and ask if that works.

scenarios.situation: Monday morning, a colleague asks about your weekend.
scenarios.task: Say two things you did, in order.

scenarios.situation: You arrive twenty minutes late to meet someone.
scenarios.task: Apologise and explain what happened.

scenarios.situation: At the doctor with a bad cold. You have an important meeting tomorrow.
scenarios.task: Ask what you should do, and say you have to work tomorrow.

scenarios.situation: You are in a restaurant and don't know a word on the menu.
scenarios.task: Ask what it means, then order it and ask for the bill later.

scenarios.situation: Your partner suggests a beach holiday. You would prefer the mountains.
scenarios.task: Say what you'd rather do, give a reason, and propose a compromise.

scenarios.situation: A discussion about working from home.
scenarios.task: Give your opinion with one reason and one concession.

scenarios.situation: You missed your train this morning.
scenarios.task: Tell the story: what had happened before, and what you did next.

scenarios.situation: Your hotel room is noisy and the wifi doesn't work.
scenarios.task: Complain politely and ask to change rooms.

scenarios.situation: A friend failed an exam because they didn't study.
scenarios.task: Say what they should have done and what you'd do in their place.

scenarios.situation: Your boss moved the deadline to Thursday and asked you to tell the team.
scenarios.task: Report what your boss said and what she asked you to do.

scenarios.situation: A debate about a four-day working week.
scenarios.task: Argue for it, concede one drawback, then counter the drawback.

scenarios.situation: A colleague didn't show up to an important meeting and isn't answering.
scenarios.task: Speculate about what must have happened and what might have happened.

scenarios.situation: You turned down a job last year and now regret it.
scenarios.task: Say what you would have done if you had known, and what you wish.

scenarios.situation: The heating in your flat has been broken for a week.
scenarios.task: Write a formal request to the landlord to have it repaired, with a deadline.

scenarios.situation: A friend asks what you think about banning cars from city centres.
scenarios.task: Summarise both sides, then give your balanced view.

scenarios.situation: Someone asks about your goals.
scenarios.task: Say what you will have achieved by this time next year, and what you'll be doing then.

scenarios.situation: In a meeting, a senior colleague proposes a plan you think is flawed.
scenarios.task: Disagree diplomatically and suggest what you would have expected instead.

scenarios.situation: You are chairing. Someone has gone off on a tangent.
scenarios.task: Cut them off politely, park the point, and return to the agenda.

scenarios.situation: A trip you had planned for months collapsed the day before.
scenarios.task: Describe it with some irony: what was to have happened and what you didn't know.

scenarios.situation: Someone claims AI will replace all translators within five years.
scenarios.task: Qualify the claim: to what extent it holds and where it fails.

scenarios.situation: A supplier has delivered late twice.
scenarios.task: Insist formally that they deliver on time, on condition that otherwise the contract be reviewed.

scenarios.situation: You finished a project and only then learned the requirements had changed.
scenarios.task: Tell it with a participle clause and an inverted opener.
